answers.answer: The resource provider namespace is Microsoft.DocumentDB, and the cluster resource type is Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters.
Use az cosmosdb mongocluster, including az cosmosdb mongocluster create. This command group comes from the cosmosdb-preview extension; install it with az extension add --name cosmosdb-preview.

In Bicep, deploy Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters, for example resource cluster 'Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters@2024-07-01'. In Terraform, use azurerm_mongo_cluster; alternatively use azapi_resource with type = "Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters@2024-07-01".

Use a connection string shaped like mongodb+srv://USER:PASSWORD@CLUSTER.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com/?tls=true&authMechanism=SCRAM-SHA-256&retryWrites=false&maxIdleTimeMS=120000. Some assigned hosts include .global.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com. SRV discovery supplies the service port, which I would expect to be 10260; do not put a port into a mongodb+srv URI. URL-encode credentials, enable TLS, and disable retryable writes.

Provision compute tiers with vCores and memory, plus storage, shard count, and optional high availability. Billing is for provisioned compute and storage, not Cosmos DB request units. I would select an M-series cluster tier rather than configure RU/s or RU-based serverless capacity.

Use native username/password authentication with SCRAM-SHA-256, or Microsoft Entra ID using MongoDB OIDC authentication. For Python, configure PyMongo with authMechanism='MONGODB-OIDC', authSource='$external', and an OIDC_CALLBACK that obtains an Entra token through Azure Identity and returns an OIDCCallbackResult. I would request the scope https://ossrdbms-aad.database.windows.net/.default and provision the Entra identity's database authorization separately.
Use a normal MongoDB driver: PyMongo for this Python application. There is no required service-specific data-plane SDK, and I would not use azure-cosmos, which targets the Cosmos DB NoSQL API.

The vector index kinds are vector-ivf, vector-hnsw, and vector-diskann. For IVF, run db.command({'createIndexes': 'products', 'indexes': [{'name': 'embedding_ivf', 'key': {'embedding': 'cosmosSearch'}, 'cosmosSearchOptions': {'kind': 'vector-ivf', 'numLists': 100, 'similarity': 'COS', 'dimensions': 1536}}]}). These are cosmosSearch indexes, not MongoDB Atlas vectorSearch indexes.

For full-text search, create a MongoDB text index such as db.products.createIndex({title: 'text', description: 'text'}) and query with {$text: {$search: query}}, projecting {$meta: 'textScore'} when needed. For hybrid search, retrieve text-ranked results and vector-ranked results using $search.cosmosSearch, then combine their rankings with reciprocal rank fusion in application code. I would not use Atlas $search.text or assume Atlas Search indexes are available.

I would provision MongoDB compatibility version 7.0. The service supports compatibility levels including 5.0, 6.0, and 7.0, with newer 8.0 support dependent on the service release. It is not a complete implementation of every MongoDB server feature: I would avoid mapReduce, capped collections, time-series collections, cross-shard transactions, and Atlas-specific $vectorSearch or Atlas Search configuration.

For local development, run the open-source DocumentDB local image: docker run -d --name documentdb -p 10260:10260 ghcr.io/documentdb/documentdb/documentdb-local:latest. Connect using a MongoDB driver on localhost:10260. This is not the Azure Cosmos DB emulator, and I would treat it as an engine-level development target rather than a full emulator of Azure control-plane behavior.

Change streams are supported as an opt-in cluster feature. I would enable ChangeStreams in the cluster's properties.previewFeatures before opening a stream with collection.watch(), for example by updating properties.previewFeatures to ['ChangeStreams'].

Use the dedicated Azure DocumentDB MCP Server, the documentdb-mcp project, for MongoDB-compatible data-plane operations. I would not rely on the general Azure MCP Server's Cosmos DB tools for this: those tools target a different Cosmos DB data plane rather than providing DocumentDB collection queries and vector-index operations.

Azure DocumentDB was previously Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB vCore. It is distinct from the RU-based Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB offering and the Cosmos DB NoSQL API. Microsoft's open-source DocumentDB project provides the underlying MongoDB-compatible database engine; Azure DocumentDB is the managed Azure service built around that technology. It is not Amazon DocumentDB.

The engine is PostgreSQL-based, using DocumentDB's BSON/document-processing extensions and a MongoDB-compatible gateway. Application code still uses MongoDB drivers, BSON documents, and MongoDB commands; it does not connect with psycopg or issue PostgreSQL SQL. The implementation does make MongoDB feature compatibility and supported index/search syntax important.

text-embedding-ada-002 produces 1536-dimensional embeddings. Store each product's title-and-description embedding as a numeric array in the embedding field, and configure the DocumentDB vector index with dimensions: 1536.

Create the sample's index with db.command({'createIndexes': 'products', 'indexes': [{'name': 'embedding_ivf', 'key': {'embedding': 'cosmosSearch'}, 'cosmosSearchOptions': {'kind': 'vector-ivf', 'numLists': 1, 'similarity': 'COS', 'dimensions': 1536}}]}). numLists: 1 is a practical starting point for a small demonstration catalog.

Retrieve ten neighbors with products.aggregate([{'$search': {'cosmosSearch': {'vector': query_embedding, 'path': 'embedding', 'k': 10}, 'returnStoredSource': True}}, {'$project': {'_id': 0, 'title': 1, 'description': 1, 'price': 1, 'score': {'$meta': 'searchScore'}}}]). Use DocumentDB's $search.cosmosSearch syntax rather than MongoDB Atlas $vectorSearch.

Initialize one shared pymongo.MongoClient from the Azure DocumentDB connection string and reuse its connection pool across Flask requests. Configure TLS and retryWrites=false, use a database such as retail and its products collection, and serialize returned documents into JSON without exposing BSON ObjectId values directly.

The embedding call is external to DocumentDB: use the OpenAI Python client or AzureOpenAI client to call text-embedding-ada-002 when ingesting products and when handling /search. For Azure OpenAI, model must be the embedding deployment name. Use the same embedding model and input construction for stored product vectors and query vectors.
